subject: Acme: intermittent p99 spikes — replay and shed thresholds
messages:

Date: Fri, 20 Apr 2028 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Production: intermittent p99 spikes impacting checkout

Hey Karthik —

We started seeing intermittent p99 spikes on our checkout route (order-processing) since ~06:30 PT. There's an uptick in 504s and timeouts; retries from our side look like normal backoff behavior but we also see a cluster of duplicate requests showing up in your traces.

Attached is a short timeline and a couple spans from the traces we could pull on our side. Can you confirm whether any shed/concurrency changes or routing policy changes were applied this morning? This is impacting a subset of accounts — ~1% of our traffic but high-value transactions.

We need an ETA on mitigation.

Thanks,
Sara
Sara Mendoza

Sara — thanks for the heads up and the logs. I'm pulling the traces now and looping in Dev and Hannah to triage.

Initial ask: can you confirm whether Acme's client SDK is enabling automatic replay on 5xx responses (no jitter) or if retries are driven from your edge? That'll help us rule out client-side replays vs server-side replay loops.

We'll aim to provide an initial mitigation within 60 minutes. If this is a shed/concurrency interaction we can both (a) temporarily increase the customer route concurrency cap and (b) tighten replay/dedup logic on our side to avoid duplicate inflight requests.

I'll update shortly with traces and proposed steps.

— Karthik
Head of Customer Reliability, Redwood Inference
From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai
Cc: sara.mendoza@acme-payments.com
Date: Fri, 20 Apr 2028 09:05:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Production: intermittent p99 spikes impacting checkout

Triage notes (quick):
- I pulled the request traces for route /v1/generate?acct=ACME-4932 between 06:15-08:15 PT.
- Observed repeated request ids (same client_request_id header) arriving ~1-2s apart for a subset of users — looks like client replay + no server-side dedupe.
- At ~06:40 PT we hit a shed threshold on the dedicated pool for the route (concurrency cap = 4). When shed triggers, the runtime falls back to queuing in the route work-queue. Queue depth spikes -> backpressure -> KV-cache pressure on long requests -> p99 climbs.
- Crucially, a small proportion of inflight failures are being auto-replayed by the request middleware (a previous change to enable transparent retries for transient infra errors). That replay behavior re-enqueues requests without checking for duplicate client_request_id, so duplicates re-enter the queue and amplify queueing/backpressure.

Attached: acme_trace_20280420.zip (trace bundle), scatter_p99.png (p99 over time with queue depth overlay).

Proposed immediate mitigations (to do in this order):
1) temporarily raise route concurrency cap from 4 -> 8 for ACME-4932 (targeted, narrow scope).
2) disable transparent server-side automatic replay for 5xx on that route (turn into 1s backoff + dedupe check) — quick config flip.
3) apply lightweight dedupe on client_request_id at ingress (drop exact matches inside 10s window).
4) add a short-term circuit-breaker on queue depth (fail fast with 429 and a clarifying retry-after) to prevent unlimited buildup while we stabilize.

I can implement 1+2 in the next 15 minutes if we have signoff. 3 requires a small hotfix (estimated 2-3 hours) and 4 needs ops approval but is low-risk.

Let me know and I'll execute.

— Dev
Senior Software Engineer, Runtime

Sara — quick update from Redwood: we are applying a targeted increase to your route concurrency cap and disabling server-side automatic replays for your account right now. Expect to see improvement in the p99 within 10–20 minutes.

Ask from our side: can your SREs temporarily disable aggressive client-side retries for the next 30 minutes (or add jitter/backoff) while we validate? If you prefer, we can also add a small header to responses indicating a recommended retry-after to help clients coordinate.

I'll update you at +30m with stabilization metrics; please ping me if you still see elevated timeouts.

— Grace O'Connor
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference
From: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
To: hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai, dev_patel@redwood.ai, grace_oconnor@redwood.ai
Cc: Sara Mendoza <sara.mendoza@acme-payments.com>
Date: Fri, 20 Apr 2028 12:45:00 -0700
Subject: Post-mortem readout: actions taken and next steps (Acme)

Summary (final):
- Actions executed: raised route concurrency cap ACME-4932 4->8 (targeted, 1 node group), disabled automatic server-side 5xx replays for the route, enabled 10s dedupe window at ingress for client_request_id for identical IDs. We also added a short-term queue-depth circuit-breaker to fail fast at 200 requests backlog with 429 + retry-after.
- Immediate impact: p99 dropped from ~1.8s to ~380ms over a 30m window; 504s down by 87% (per attached scatter_p99.png). No broad perf regressions observed.
- Follow-ups (owners/timeline):
  * Dev: push dedupe hotfix to staging + prod rollout with canary (ETA 3 hours) — dev_patel@redwood.ai
  * Hannah: update runbook to include dedupe + circuit-break thresholds (ETA 2 business days) — hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai
  * Grace/Karthik: discuss whether a permanent route-level cap increase or adaptive scaling policy is appropriate (decision in 3 business days).

Exec note: this incident was customer-impacting and driven by a combination of client replays and a tight route concurrency cap that caused queue buildup and amplified duplicates. The runtime behaved as designed for shed -> queue fallback, but the replay behavior without dedupe created an amplification loop. We will push the dedupe fix and a runbook change to prevent recurrence.

If leadership wants a short briefing with numbers / charts, I can prepare a 15-minute readout.

Thanks all — closing the loop.

— Karthik
Head of Customer Reliability, Redwood Inference
